page: Amazon Web Services c6id.large is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8375C processor operating at 3.5 GHz using the x86_64 architecture, providing 2 vCPUs across 1 physical core with 2 execution threads. The instance is configured with 4.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, maintaining a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio. Ephemeral local storage is bundled directly on the instance via a 118 GB NVMe SSD, and network connectivity operates at a baseline of 1 Gbps. Hardware-level instruction support includes AVX-512 with VNNI, AES-NI, and SHA extensions.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent single-core execution alongside predictable multi-core scaling limitations. In single-threaded CPU benchmarks, the system achieved a Geekbench score of 1607.0 and a stress-ng score of 1879.79, representing mid-tier single-core throughput. Multi-core performance is constrained by the two-thread capacity, posting a Geekbench multi-core score of 1852.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 2992.99. Memory subsystem throughput for large 256MB blocks measured 14.19 GB/sec for uncached reads and 13.42 GB/sec for writes, resulting in modest throughput for data-dense operations.

The presence of local NVMe storage delivers high input and output capability for temporary data without requiring external block volume attachments. However, total memory capacity of 4.0 GB and baseline networking limit suitability for high-concurrency or horizontally scaled architectures. The instance is suited for localized compilation steps, lightweight continuous integration workers, batch utilities, and intermediate scratch processing that rely on fast local disk access.
description: Amazon Web Services c6id.large is a compute-optimized virtual instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Managed by the Nitro hypervisor, it allocates 2 vCPUs from 1 dedicated physical core and features 4.0 GB of DDR4 system memory alongside a bundled 118 GB local NVMe SSD. Single-threaded performance reaches mid-range marks with a Geekbench single-core score of 1607.0 and gzip compression at 27.91 GB/sec. However, overall multi-core throughput and memory bandwidth remain modest due to the two-thread execution envelope and sub-15 GB/sec uncached transfer rates. Network capacity is bounded at a 1 Gbps baseline. Lacking a discrete GPU, the c6id.large is designed for workloads requiring direct-attached, low-latency NVMe scratch space and steady single-core CPU throughput, such as lightweight software builds, continuous integration runners, intermediate data transformation, and small-scale web serving.
